To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have developed and validated a set of reference gene for qPCR analysis in grasses.
we identified a set of reference gene for grasses.
we have identified a set of reference (housekeeping) genes that can be used to normalise gene expression studies in grasses.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the identification of a reference gene set that can be used to normalise gene expression data in grasses, a group of plants that is of major agronomic and economic importance and for which genomic resources are still lacking.
improving the efficiency of the qPCR technology to study gene expression in grasses, which are of great importance in the agricultural and environmental sciences.
the development of tools that are useful in studies aimed at understanding the mechanisms of resistance to herbicides in Alopecurus and other grasses.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the reference gene set (Ubiquitin, beta-Tubulin and GAPDH) proposed in this study should be used for the normalisation of qPCR data in grasses.
the set of reference genes proposed in this study is a good choice for qPCR data normalisation in grass species, including A. myosuroides.
the set of reference genes described here is a good candidate for studies seeking to analyse the expression of genes involved in the response to herbicides in grasses.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
this study provides a set of reference gene candidates for qPCR studies in grass species.
the use of a set of genes with a stable expression is essential in qPCR-based studies of gene expression in grasses.
the reference genes identified here are suitable for qPCR data normalization of grasses in the presence or absence of herbicides, and for studies of gene expression under herbicide-stress conditions.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of reference genes for normalising qPCR expression data should be based on a validation study using a panel of candidate reference genes and the complementary statistical methods available.
the use of a single reference gene for normalisation in qPCR experiments is not recommended, and the use of a set of genes is strongly encouraged.
reference gene validation must be performed for every new biological system and experimental conditions.
